correctness.rationale: The 35-state generator and its five rotation classes are explicitly enumerated. The stationary distribution solves the column generator balance with unit sum for all positive q. Differentiating the tilted generator, solving its normalized Poisson equation, and symbolic rational elimination prove the two cumulants. Every coefficient of P is positive, and direct leading-term algebra proves the asymptotic ratio 2. The packaged checker reproduces the exact symbolic identities and independently checks the unreduced 35-state system at q=1/2 and q=2. Finite checks alone are not used for the all-parameter claim.

originality.rationale: The exact seven-site second signed-current cumulant and its ratio 2 in the strong-forward-bias limit were not identified in the full-text inspection of the motivating paper, whose Figure 2 presents the mean current. The other closely relevant full texts cover equilibrium half-filled area variance or a different Fredkin kinetic constraint and activity fluctuations. Indexed related finite-ring results concern other generators or total activity; none entails the stated rational function without a new observable-specific generator computation. This is a qualified priority judgment, not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unindexed or implicit equivalent computation of the same seven-site signed-current SCGF could supersede the claimed priority.
The explicit finite-state computation may be viewed as a specialized application of well-known perturbation theory; conceptual reach is limited to the natural minimal model.
Independent expert comparison and validation have not been performed.

value.rationale: The three-particle seven-site ring is the first active finite cluster-forming benchmark of the motivating faster-is-slower dynamics, whose published exact mean curves do not determine noise. The positive exact full-rate variance and nontrivial strong-drive Fano 2 quantify bursty temporal transport in a physically motivated minimal model and provide an analytically reproducible diagnostic for simulations; this is a natural dynamical invariant, not a randomly selected parameter sample. The theorem makes no unsupported thermodynamic-limit inference.
